reasons.v3/admission_a13.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): binding() and verify() accept the new admission scope 'A10_nominal_after_A14' beside the two A13 scopes. Every Part 2 condition is unchanged: the floor(N/1000) cap, one admitted row per context, the balanced-witness exclusion, the item 12(b) screens and the re-test violation refusal. Only the A14 publication writes that scope. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds. Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then added A16's two stage 2 admission scopes, which require bound family and round provenance carrying the item 10 record identities, and a marker check over every row of the candidate: a stage 2 row never carries the nominal marker, a violation in either round refuses admission whatever the row's status, and round 2 cannot hide round 1's marker. A13 Part 2's own conditions, caps, limits and bindings are unchanged and every nominal scope behaves exactly as before.
reasons.v3/artifacts.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): adds A14_COMMIT 17f17ef9. Current (non-historical) A10 launches and publications verify strictly against 17f17ef9, whose design note must contain the A13 clarification and '### Amendment A14' and match the working note byte for byte; plans pinned to 48815a65 or earlier, including A13's, verify historically by ancestry and committed bytes. Digest, seal, canonical JSON, seed and job-identity functions are unchanged. A2 re-pinned (68c30205 to cb526190, recorded under a14). Classification of the A14 change: A14 stated exception: the current-pin change. Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then generalized the current A10 pin into the shared helpers current_a10_commit, is_current_a10_pin, current_a10_note_markers and a13_binding_pins so the three pin sites move together, moved the current pin to the A17 adoption commit 3b8d8261 while keeping A16's ae71028e and A13's and A14's commits bound in both forms, added A16's and A17's headings to the exact-note markers, and closed a Windows-only containment race in scoped() by comparing without the extended-length prefix. The POSIX containment statements are unchanged by that revision, and digest, seal, canonical JSON, seed and job-identity functions are unchanged throughout. The A11 historical-view repair (55b7b4a6), authorized by amendment A18, then added historical_view, a context-scoped declaration of existing historical copy trees outside this checkout, and one early return in scoped() for a path under a declared root that is an existing directory or an existing file with no write bit set. A sealed history inventory freezes each copy destination as an absolute path inside the checkout that staged it, so a producing identity that carries a history could not be loaded at a successor identity at all, which is where a compatibility proof runs; history_a14.py equals the A17 commit 74460801 and history_a16.py equals 7f793c75, which introduced it, after newline normalization, and both keep hashing every copy and requiring it read-only. Resolution is not permission to write: atomic_json, lease, snapshot_a11.receive and compatibility_shards_a11.stage_inputs resolve through write_scoped, which refuses a declared root outright, and worker_safety's metadata_json and persist_restarts write through atomic_json. compatibility_shards_a11.write_once needs no guard, creating exclusively, so it cannot replace a copy that exists. No claim is made that nothing in the tree can write under a declared root. Four claims of that shape were made in succession and a blind review refuted each: resolution alone, a complete writer list, an enforced declaration scope, and a parsed resolver inventory. A reviewer on a different model named the pattern rather than the instance, that each version turned a syntactic observation into a semantic guarantee, so what follows is stated as fact about the code and nothing more. About 126 calls across 88 module-and-function pairs resolve a path through scoped. Which of them write is not recorded, because resolving is not evidence either way: table_validation_a4.publish resolves and then writes through atomic_json, so it is guarded, while budget_a6.append_consumption and service.command are not, and guarding every writer would be a tree-wide change touching several A2 boundary files. The declaration is used at one site, replay_a16.original_validation_plan, and three independent reviews read that recovery path and found it writes nothing. simulation/scoped_call_sites.json records the resolver call sites as they stand at this identity, verified exact by an independent traversal of the production modules. The tests over that inventory and over the named helpers are regression tripwires on the text, not proofs about behaviour: a getattr, a container subscript, an annotated rebinding, a cross-module re-export, or an if-False guard before a bare resolve all pass them, and the behavioural assertions that call each guarded helper against a real declared root are the evidence those helpers refuse. The guards bind at resolution time and promise nothing about filesystem changes after a path has been resolved. The residual that cannot be closed is history_a14.stage_history and history_a16.stage_history, frozen under their suite pins, which write and chmod through scoped. They are not symmetric: A16 confines every destination to the view root it is given and refuses anything outside it, while A14 takes no view-root argument at all and checks destinations only against source paths, original directories and protected anchors. A proof constructs History rather than staging, so neither is called on the proof path. A missing or writable copy still refuses, no declared root may overlap this checkout, and with nothing declared the branch cannot be taken, so containment outside an A11 proof is the reviewed base: test_review_output_scope_matches_base checks that statement for statement outside the two carved branches, and the declaration's own refusals are checked in test_v3_stage2_phase2. Two earlier versions of this repair stated this wrongly and are recorded so a reader is not misled: the first claimed resolution itself made a declared root read-only, which a blind review refuted by writing through atomic_json, because a 0444 mode does not prevent os.replace rewriting a directory entry whose parent is writable; the second named only the frozen stagers as residual and claimed both confine destinations to a given view root, which a second blind review refuted on both counts. Amendment A19 (2026-11-04) then made configure_threads also set the live OpenBLAS limit through the library's own setter when numpy is already imported. It never imports numpy, so a fresh worker still configures before the library starts, and runtime() verifies the effective limit as before.
reasons.v3/compatibility_a10.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): _execute_proof routes a selected a13_validate_plain_ext job that carries an a13_replay binding to replay_a14.replay, the isolated re-simulation of every recorded replicate from its seed in an empty scratch root with each checkpoint compared; collect_record attaches that binding (plan, job, recorded result, checkpoint documents) to selected A13-phase jobs and, for the sealed single-host registered A13 plan, takes the scheduling class from the hash-bound original validation plan (worker_seconds x R_max/3); build_record passes the proof sources' declared historical roots to the single-host preflight. Population, stratum, selection, comparison bytes, before/after hashes, record fields and approval are unchanged, and ordinary execution cannot reach the replay path. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds (the authorized compatibility-replay adapter); A14 stated exception: the snapshot-path repair (declared roots). Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then routed the A14 and A16 extension kinds through the explicit empty-scratch replay adapters in proofs and scaled the original validation plan's scheduling class by R_max over 3 for registered single-host plans. The comparison rule, the selection rule, the excluded metadata fields and the record schema are unchanged. The A11 historical-view repair (55b7b4a6) then passes the sources' declared historical roots from collect_record into that original validation plan read, and records them in the record's execution metadata as historical_view with their provenance; and adds preflight_record, the assembly a build performs before it executes anything (the sources and their registration, the reasons against the live source diff, each producing identity's bindings and sealed history, the sample, the configuration profiles and every selected job's declared inputs), which writes nothing, creates no attempt and spends no reservation, so a batch clears every record it intends to build before the first proof runs. The preflight is not a launch gate: host admission, the settings and CPU check, live memory and qualified class reservations, snapshot reception, thread verification, the configuration test and a dispatch's source-pin verification all come later and can still refuse. It refuses a planned record whose attempt or reservation is already spent while no completed record exists, which is terminal under 17.3, rather than reporting it after the siblings have run. "Completed" is checked rather than assumed from existence: the target must unseal to a record of this schema with passed true and this identity pair, because a blind review found that an existence test alone accepted an empty file, a directory or a half-written record and would have waved the spent attempt through. The populations and strata, the selection rule, the comparison bytes, the before and after hashes and the record schema are unchanged; the record gains two execution-metadata fields, historical_view and historical_view_provenance, which no named-field consumer reads, though whole-record serialization and sealing of course include them. Amendment A19 (2026-11-04) then binds, for each rerun job of a registered source, the historically verified registration as that job's proof authority, which _execute_proof sets around that one job and resets, each context variable with its own reset, so a proof's succession gates decide as the registered run's did. collect_record now hashes each source spec once and reads a registered extension spec's original plan once, assembling the same record, and build_record records the operating mode, worker cap and thread count the build was launched with in place of collect_record's placeholder; live control changes stay in the worker-control and scheduling records. Selection, comparison and validation are unchanged.
reasons.v3/compatibility_shards_a11.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): source_historical_roots() unions each proof source's declared absolute historical_roots with any roots frozen in its spec; portable_inventory() refuses a proof input outside the checkout or those roots before staging and seals the roots and their hash into the inventory; stage_inputs() re-verifies that scope; qualification_bundle(), freeze() and single_preflight() carry the same roots, so qualification and the proof use identical declarations. Selection, comparison, scheduling, the identity-pair reservation and finality are unchanged. Classification of the A14 change: A14 stated exception: the snapshot-path repair. The A11 historical-view repair (55b7b4a6) then routes stage_inputs through write_scoped rather than scoped, so a declared historical root is refused as a staging destination even though it resolves for the history verifiers. A blind review found it by probe: stage_inputs resolved through scoped and then reached mkdir, shutil.copyfile and an unconditional chmod on a declared historical copy. write_once is deliberately left unguarded, creating exclusively, so it cannot replace a copy that exists. Nothing else in this module changes: the shard freeze, staging, scheduling, the identity-pair reservation and finality are all as before. Amendment A19 (2026-11-04) then made the proof's memory waits wait and report instead of raising. run_items no longer raises after PROOF_MEMORY_WAIT_SECONDS when no proof job is running and the smallest pending job does not fit; it reports the wait in its scheduling status and dispatches as soon as the job fits. A shard's preflight memory waits after its attempt is reserved have no time limit either, while the single-host preflight, before any reservation, keeps its 180-second refusal. _combine records each host's mode, worker count and thread count as its shard result reports them, in place of collect_record's placeholder; at top level, a mode and a thread count only where every host agrees, and the total worker count when every host reports one. Scheduling order, admission, the proofs and the combine binding are unchanged.
reasons.v3/forecast_a14.py: New A14 module (item 6): stages a read-only 55817036 source view from git blobs; validates the sealed forecast configuration (interpreter, Python and numpy versions, package paths outside the checkout); runs the three hash-pinned assessment scripts unchanged in an isolated -I -B interpreter with repository-import and data-path guards and inventory-mapped reads; returns only the two round-2 probabilities with environment and hash records (exit 78 is a finding). Used only by A14 preparation and preentry; no estimation, validation or proof path imports it. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds.
reasons.v3/forecast_a16.py: New module. A16 item 6's predicted admission probability before each round's go: the family-general adapter of A14's model, with the seed as the low 60 bits of the canonical JSON hash, 4,000 draws fixed when registered, and every simulated status passed through the unchanged Part 2 predicates. It runs no simulation and draws no registered stream. It is a root module, so it is in the source manifest and contributes to this code identity, and the estimates it produces are recorded in the A16 plan and its public record.
reasons.v3/history_a14.py: New A14 module (item 1): the roles-based sealed history inventory builder (read-only, hash-verified copies with aliases) and the read-only verifier, which recomputes A13 eligibility and classifications from the copies and checks the A13 round, the original refusal and the committed compatibility records; it writes nothing on failure. Used only by A14 preparation and preentry. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds. Phase 2 (7f793c75) adds a caller without changing this file: the successor's replay_a16 adapter imports History to recover the original validation plan for a compatibility proof. A14's own launch validation and publication also call verify_history, so the earlier statement that it is used only by A14 preparation and pre-entry no longer bounds its use.
reasons.v3/history_a16.py: New module. A16 items 1 and 7: the read-only verifier and inventory builder for a family's original records, parallel to history_a14, which copies inventoried inputs by hash into a declared view outside the registered trees, recomputes the first round's per-row classifications from the sealed evidence, and refuses any destination on a protected anchor, inside a registered tree, inside a historical root or outside the declared view root. It reads completed outputs and writes none.
reasons.v3/host_a11.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): execute_scratch() gains an a14_validate_plain_ext2 branch with its own checkpoint context and a round-2 scientific-halt marker; run_host() transfers that kind's durable replicate checkpoints (a14_checkpoint) and reports a14_halt for it. A13 and every other kind follow their existing paths unchanged. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds (dispatch). Amendment A19 (2026-11-04) then made a host's configuration trials dispatch against the launch deadline the coordinator reports, refusing to start a trial when it reports none, and record their elapsed time against configuration_seconds as a planning figure, on a failure as well as on success; a loopback max_seconds still bounds the trials. Scientific job handling is unchanged.
reasons.v3/multihost_a11.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): ALLOWED_KINDS adds a14_validate_plain_ext2; freeze() refuses registered A14 (single-host only) and gives the kind the R_max/3 ordering weight; prepare() binds the A14 round; the coordinator latches A14 halts, hands out A14 durable checkpoints in claims, accepts a14_checkpoint and a14_halt (added to the RPC allowlist) and latches nondeterminism for that kind. Snapshot-path repair: freeze() accepts --historical-root (or the spec's declared roots) and seals the roots and their hash into pull_dispatch, validate_extension() checks them, and the coordinator's phase snapshots use them. Claims, comparisons and checks for other kinds are unchanged. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds (dispatch); A14 stated exception: the snapshot-path repair. Amendment A19 (2026-11-04) then made the wall and charged allowances dispatch stops only. A host's hard stop is now the operator's interruption or a lost coordinator, and the coordinator stays until every open session has ended, so the clock cuts off neither a running lease nor a host's configuration trials, and the participation ledger charges the drain. A job leased before the stop and finished after it is recorded like any other; the cutoff is lease admission. The launch records the stop's reason, deadline or charged_allowance, and its drain with the overrun, ending when no lease is active and no session is open; a join after that is refused. The phase projection refuses only before the launch's first scientific lease and is recorded as advisory after it, and the status reports the launch deadline that hosts' configuration trials dispatch against. Leasing, comparison, duplicate checks and halts are unchanged.
reasons.v3/pilot_a10.py: Audit A finding 8, execution provenance only: the A7 and R4 ceiling comparison in the cost pilot's projection is renamed a7_r4_a6_ceiling_x2_hours and a6_within_a7_r4_ceiling and carries an explicit scope string, so it cannot be read as stage 2 budget authority, which A15 supplies. The projection's output keys therefore change. No pilot seed, job, sample or arithmetic changes, and the registered pilot's completed outputs are not rewritten.
reasons.v3/production_runner.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): execute() dispatches a14_validate_plain_ext2 (non-registered only as a rehearsal or configuration test with non-reserved seeds); the a13_validate_plain_ext branch first routes an authorized replay (replay_a14.authorized_replay, true only inside the proof adapter's context for that job and scratch root) to execute_replay; worker() and the nondeterminism check latch the A14 round; validate_spec() verifies A14 specs inside their declared execution inputs; a guard rejects the A14 reserved range [2^61, 2^62) for every non-A14 job; launch() binds the A14 round, refuses a latched A14 halt, and memory-manages and rechecks the A14 phase; calibration loading covers the new kind. A2 re-pinned (e9fe15b9 to 0d3f5f3c, recorded under a14). The scientific execute paths of existing kinds, outputs, completion and checkpoint writes are unchanged. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds (dispatch, the replay adapter, and the A14 reserved-range guard, which no existing job seed meets). Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then added parallel branches for the two A16 kinds only: their dispatch with the rehearsal and configuration rule and every reserve refused for non-registered work, the explicit empty-scratch replay adapters for the A14 and A16 kinds used by compatibility proofs, the worker's and the recheck's scientific-halt latches, A16 plan validation and round binding at launch, the A16 schema in the memory-managed and recheck sets, and a reserved-range guard that refuses an A16 reserve seed on any non-A16 job. It also added a per-kind qualification coverage check inside qualified_hosts, which the load-sheet command calls when it is given host entries; that check is not a launch gate and the launch branch does not call it. Existing scientific execution and ordinary result payloads are unchanged. Amendment A19 (2026-11-04) then gave the rerun branch, when not registered, the guard authority compatibility_a10.proof_authority returns, which exists only inside an A11 proof, only for a rerun from a registered source and only for the job it is bound to; outside a proof it returns nothing and the branch is unchanged. It also made a launch's deadline a dispatch stop. No job starts after it; every running job finishes and is recorded, with the drain and its overrun recorded; and the launch ends incomplete unless the drain finished every remaining job and check. The operator's interruption, a signal or interrupt_now, still stops workers at once, and reaches the nondeterminism recheck whether it is paused or running. A finished result is no longer discarded after its completion deadline; a per-phase projection refuses only before the launch's first scientific dispatch and is advisory after it; configuration trials dispatch against the launch deadline, with configuration_seconds recorded as a planning figure; and a recheck that the dispatch stop or an operator stop kept from running to a comparison is recorded as not run, with no failure file and no halt latch. A recheck that runs is compared and a mismatch halts as before. The scientific execution of each job and its result payload are unchanged; what changes is scheduling at the deadline and what the launch records.
reasons.v3/production_tables.py: Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then added A16 item 8's loader cross-check of a bound admission's family against the manifest's family, the receipt policy keyed by validated family identity so the three A6 variant families are accepted only with an authenticated no-label receipt while nominal and sqrt keep the strict A5 checks, and a refusal to load any admission whose A16 provenance carries a hypothetical marker. The numerical lookup, the row statuses and the support and sensitivity gates are unchanged.
reasons.v3/qualification_a11.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): a14_validate_plain_ext2 qualifies from non-registered short fixture streams (seeds at or above 2^128), as A13 does; build() passes the spec's declared historical roots to the inventory, copies each bundle file from its verified source with hash checks before and after copying, and makes external or aliased copies read-only. The X2-1 reference rule, the comparison and the evidence fields used for approval are unchanged. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds; A14 stated exception: the snapshot-path repair. Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then requires at least 20 distinct reference jobs per kind rather than 20 pooled across kinds (A17 section 2(b) and section 6 item 2), added an optional kinds argument so a caller can require coverage of named kinds, and admitted the A16 kinds to the short-test build with non-reserved streams. The only caller that passes kinds is the load-sheet host check, so the coverage requirement is not enforced at launch. Historical evidence that met the pooled rule and not the per-kind rule now fails, which is the intended tightening.
reasons.v3/reading_a6.py: A12 part 1 item 7 and the stage 2 reader contract: compare_boundary takes an explicit undefined-resample tail, defaulting to A6's 0.05/66, records it in the result and in the undefined-resample reason string, and validates it as a probability. The default reproduces the pinned arithmetic exactly, and the boundary rule, the interval arithmetic, the margins and the resampling order are unchanged.
reasons.v3/replay_a14.py: New A14 module, the compatibility-replay adapter (step 2): binds an A13 plan job, its recorded result and checkpoint documents; is authorized only inside the proof's producer context for that job and an empty scratch root; re-simulates each recorded replicate from its seed with A13's unchanged extension_stage and requires byte-identical checkpoints. It never resumes the A13 root, loads a checkpoint as completed work, derives a statistic, or writes a family record. It is the only exception to the reserved-seed guard, limited to the A13 plan's own jobs and seeds. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds (the authorized proof adapter; unreachable from ordinary execution).
reasons.v3/replay_a16.py: New module. The explicit empty-scratch replay adapters for the A14 and A16 extension kinds, used only by a compatibility proof: each recorded replicate is re-simulated from its recorded seed in an empty scratch root with the producer's unchanged extension stage, recorded checkpoints are compared and never installed as completed work, and the authorization is limited to the bound plan's own job and scratch root. A13's kind keeps replay_a14. It also reads the original validation plan through history_a14's History. The A11 historical-view repair (55b7b4a6) gives original_validation_plan the proof sources' declared historical roots, so a producing identity whose sealed history staged its copies inside its own checkout loads at the successor identity, through that same unchanged verifier, which still requires every copy to be read-only and hash-exact; and adds to the A14 branch the binding the A13 and A16 branches already make, that the original plan the scheduling class is taken from is the one the frozen specification names. That binding is an added refusal on a path that previously had none and changes no job, seed or comparison byte. This function is also the sole production caller of the declaration, which is what bounds every unguarded writer elsewhere in the tree. An empty declaration, which every non-proof caller passes, leaves containment unchanged. The replay adapters, the checkpoint comparison and the reserved-seed authorization are unchanged.
reasons.v3/sensitivity_a6.py: Audit A finding 8, execution provenance only: A6's three R4 run-spec builders refuse an A10 stage table path, so a stage 2 arm cannot be built through the R4 path that carries A7's ceiling. No A6 quantity, seed, registry or completed output changes, and the builders behave identically for every R4 path.
reasons.v3/snapshot_a11.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): dependencies() takes A14 phase inputs only from each job's declared hash-verified copies; normalize_historical_roots(), historical_roots() and verify_historical_scope() bound external inputs and aliases to explicitly declared, hashed absolute roots; inventory() keeps the exact pre-A14 row layout and bytes for in-checkout inputs, stages external inputs at v3/historical_inputs/<digest>/<name> with source and aliases, and refuses undeclared roots and destination collisions; fetch() and receive() re-verify scope, and receive() rejects conflicting aliases and protects declared roots. The step 3 rehearsal confirmed unchanged in-checkout staging at both identities and the external branch on two hosts. Classification of the A14 change: A14 stated exception: the snapshot-path repair. Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then added an explicit read-only input inventory for the A16 kinds with verified aliases and no undeclared path fallback, including the nominal calibration parent that a sigma family's variant calibration validation reads. Existing kinds keep their dependency enumeration, resolved through the same input view. The A11 historical-view repair (55b7b4a6) adds historical_root_provenance, which separates the declared roots reached through a sealed source specification, hash-bound by that specification's historical_roots_sha256, from those supplied by the plain sources document, which are normalized and nothing more; the record keeps the two apart instead of asserting that every root is specification-bound, which the first version of this repair claimed and a blind review found false. The helper does not itself read identity.json: collect_record separately requires each source root's identity.json to carry the producing code hash and the specification's own digest, so the identity binding holds for a successful record collection rather than for the helper in isolation. It also routes the two write targets in receive through write_scoped, so a declared historical root cannot be written even while it resolves. normalize_historical_roots, historical_roots, verify_historical_scope, the inventory, the hashing, the read-only copies and every existing refusal are unchanged, and widening the declared set widens only where a read may resolve: no unverified byte is admitted, because every history copy is size- and hash-checked by the History verifier and every proof input by the portable inventory.
reasons.v3/table_compatibility_A2.json: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): a new a14 entry re-pins exactly artifacts.py (68c30205 to cb526190) and production_runner.py (e9fe15b9 to 0d3f5f3c), with their previous hashes, design commit 17f17ef9 and dated reasons; approved_boundary_sha256 changes for those two only, and every other pinned dependency stays exact. Classification of the A14 change: A14 stated exception: the current-pin change (its A2 re-pin record; the production_runner re-pin records the A14-only branch). Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then added the stage2_phase1 block re-pinning artifacts.py and the stage2_phase2 block re-pinning artifacts.py, production_runner.py and production_tables.py, each with its previous and new LF hashes, its reason and the scope statement that it admits no producer. The record's earlier blocks, the approved boundary for every other file and the calibration provenance are unchanged. The A11 historical-view repair (55b7b4a6) then adds the a11_historical_view block, re-pinning artifacts.py alone (f8baaa17 to 3b3d4674) with its previous hash, the amendment that authorizes it and its reason; approved_boundary_sha256 moves that one entry. The authority is amendment A18 rather than A14: the first version of this block cited A17's adoption commit 3b8d8261 on the reading that this was the same species as A14's snapshot-path exception, and a blind review found that reading unestablished, because A14 stages copies inside the authorized write scope while this resolves paths outside it, and A14 states that A14 alone admits its exception. The block records its own fourth revision and the full chain of intermediate artifacts.py hashes, each read back from its commit, because three successive blind reviews each refuted a write-safety claim and the repair moved with every one; previous_approved_sha256 stays the pre-amendment hash because the block documents one amendment, not each commit of it. The boundary set is unchanged, the other six boundary files and every other pinned dependency stay exact, and the block admits no producer. The record is itself in the source manifest, so this re-pin is part of the successor identity, and verified_record() passes again, which it did not while the boundary hash was stale. Amendment A19 (2026-11-04) then adds the a19_proof_authority block, re-pinning production_runner.py and artifacts.py with their previous and new LF hashes; the other five boundary files stay exact and the block admits no producer.
reasons.v3/table_labels_a5.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): assert_a5_seeds() forbids the widened reserved range [2^60, 2^62), covering both extension rounds (A5's existing reader already forbids both manifests through the receipt's union extension_seed_manifest); registered publication decides strict versus historical pin verification by A14_COMMIT. The A5 streams, labels, receipts and arithmetic are unchanged.
reasons.v3/table_validation_a4.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): selection sites only: publish() decides strict versus historical verification by A14_COMMIT, and prospective A13 admission applies to plans pinned to 48815a65 or 17f17ef9, so A14-pinned later validation families keep A13 Part 2's binding. No fit, validation, census or estimation function changes. Classification of the A14 change: A14 stated exception: the current-pin change (selection sites). Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then took its current-pin selection and its A13 Part 2 binding from the shared helpers, writes the refused candidate, its cell results and its compatibility receipt into the run root before re-raising a Part 2 refusal, which A16's coordinated-change clause requires and which leaves the final target untouched, and enforces the family-path clause's fixed target and calibration strings for a registered stage 2 family. On the registered path the target is now resolved earlier and two publication-guard calls are added; the successful publication write sequence and every validation quantity are unchanged.
reasons.v3/tables_a10.py: Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then added the committed stage 2 run-spec builder and the A10-aware global seed registry, froze the family-path clause's four publication targets and three calibration strings as asserted constants in the registered builder, and added the authenticated no-label receipt for the three A6 variant families with the adopted authority text, refusing the A5 receipt path for them. Stage 1's builder, its jobs, seeds and outputs are unchanged.
reasons.v3/validation_extension_a14.py: New A14 module: the second and final extension round - invocation validation and the preliminary reservation, historical verification, eligibility, constants, pricing and the R_max floor of 24, the seed manifest in [2^61, 2^61 + 2^60) with its collision check, ordered replicates from 20 with durable checkpoints, the first-N* test on this round's data alone, the halt latch, decline, preentry, two-round reassembly and publication with both round bindings. It reuses A13's unchanged numerical stage, sample-size expression and test, and is not part of any completed estimation, validation or A13 computation. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds.
reasons.v3/validation_extension_a16.py: New module. A16's prospective two-round validation extension for the four A10 stage 2 families: the two job kinds and phases, the per-family seed blocks at 2^62 + (2f + q - 1) x 2^60 with the tagged truncated hash, the reserve [2^62, 12 x 2^60) and its occupancy rule, the sealed class pricing with the floor of 6 and the cap of 32, the unchanged A13 test and stop on the round's own ordered pairs with round 2's ordinals re-based, two-round re-assembly, the family and round anchors with monotonic lifecycle and an append-only classified failure log, halts, finality and the launch allowance as the 48 hour ceiling less reserves and incurred charges. No completed A10 computation executes any of it: estimation, validation, census, label and run jobs reach only its RESERVED constant, which production_runner imports to refuse an A16 reserve seed on a non-A16 job, and its trajectory execution is confined to the two A16 kinds by the dispatch branches.
reasons.v3/worker_control.py: A14 revision (8b176c73, identity 174ab660; the A14 build and its three review-fix rounds): arithmetic_class() and configuration_resources() recognize the v3-A14-extension-1 schema and a14_ kinds for memory classification, exactly as for A13. No job, seed, setting, result, selection or comparison is read or changed. Classification of the A14 change: A14-only branch, inert for earlier kinds (memory classification of the new schema; executor, scheduling or dispatch only). For precision, the retained claim to read no job or setting is too broad: memory classification reads the job configuration and the spec's settings, copying them before it adjusts its calculation. It changes neither. Phase 1 of the stage 2 successor build (50a3d096, 2ced87ba) and phase 2 (7f793c75) then added the A16 schema to the arithmetic class and configuration resource mappings, beside A14's, so A16 jobs are memory managed like the other extension kinds. No existing class, cap, reservation or measurement changes.
